text: I opted to pay 0.89 and then after declining every single offer I'm apparently subscribed to pay 35+ a month? Absolutely not. These types of hidden costs are disgraceful seeing as the target demographic is people with ADHD. Hoping people don't notice or forget are we?

Rubbish. More disorganised and chaotic than inside my adhd brain. No help whatsoever. Unsurprisingly, when I tried to cancel my subscription it wouldn't let me confirm my identity with either my google account or email. I had to reset my password and start again. Perservence paid off and I got out before I paid anything, but its clearly designed to scam adhders by making it impossible to cancel. Total waste of my time.

Be careful about signing up on their website instead of in-app. idk when or why I did that, but it means you won't see your subscription in the play store and you won't get much in the way of reminders about it. I've been paying them $40 every 3 months since May and not realizing it and now I apparently can't refund any of it, not even the one charged TODAY. Not great for an app for ADHDers who are known to be a chronic sign up and forget demographic. 0 stars.

I never even signed up but was charged! be careful in partaking in random quizzes online. this app is preying on the forgetfulness and financial illiteracy of ADHD folks! edit: I have to now download an app I've never used to delete my subscription? seems fishy.

I was sad to discover that the app is not, in fact, free. You have to pay for the trial to even try it! I admit, at minimum it was $1, but a trial should cost nothing. Given that this app is geared towards people with ADHD, who are notoriously forgetful and not necessarily the best at managing money, I find that the paid trial automatically starting a recurring subscription, which is likely to be forgotten, to be sleazy and underhanded, taking advantage of those issues. Shameful.

I subscribed to both Fabulous and Clarify, assuming that cancelling Fabulous would cancel both since Clarify is owned by them. I was wrong and charged $55.99 twice for Clarify ($111.98 total). When I requested a refund, they refused. The app itself is poorly designed, with distracting visual and sound effects that defeat its purpose of aiding focus for ADHD. Misleading practices and a bad product—this feels like a scam. Avoid at all costs.

I do not recommend this app if you are just shopping around. If you are willing to buy from the start maybe it's for u. I tried the 1$ free trial and it is ridiculous, it is not fit for everyones schedule. Yes, I understand that ADHD is a big enemy of time but it should allow you to set your own time or give u at least 2 to 3 options for time set for schedules. But not my biggest issue with these ppl. My problem was trying to cancle my subscription they make it ridicules to even find were to.🤬

I canceled the umbrella membership but I keep getting charges and I'm still listed as a "premium member" It's incredibly frustrating and pretty scammy to make it so hard for adhders to cancel a membership

Def felt like this app, like many for adhd out there, unfortunately, is a bit predatory and takes advantage of many of the struggles that come with being adhd. Like time blindness and forgetting to cancel free trials. Money management issues and impulsivity. Being overwhelmed trying to adult at times for me personally and trying to figure out how to cancel my subscription was a pain and not even on the app. Be carefull yall. An if yall cant do better as an app then you shouldnt have one.

UPDATE: I went on the website and cancled my membership before the trial was over. They still charged me $45. They also did not respond to my email for a refund. I started using Fabulous because I need to get my (ADD) life in order. When they promoted their app for ADHD, I was excited. It's pretty... but I can't figure out what it is supposed to do other than waste my time. Fabulous is routing me well... this did nothing.

DO NOT DOWNLOAD THIS APP, they have not human service at all. They took the money from my subscription but never activated it and even though It has been a month writing to their support service asking for help or refund, it has been impossible to get a human to look into my case. They send the same automatic instructions that are of any use to my case and never a person of the support team contacted me. This app is good to exploit everything that hurts and annoy a person with ADHD.

The app is what it needs to be. But the customer service is useless. The app doesn't give you heads up when your subscription is due so I ended up paying for 2 months the monthly fee. C'mon, I have ADHD. The support refused my request for a refund even though I contacted them the same day I was charged and requested a yearly subscription. Their app is frustrating and it needs to be but support service could provide support. I will go through my card company to claim refund.

Beware - purports to help neurodiverse people. Does not. . I signed up for the “free” trial but found this app and it’s constant notifications just another thing to add stress to my day. It wasn’t particularly user friendly - the app was tricky to navigate and incessant adds and prompts to upgrade and add this and that were annoying. I cancelled my subscription- even giving the overwhelm I expressed as my reasoning, yet was still charged the monthly subscription fee with no recourse for receiving a refund (against policy apparently). I believe they’re capitalising on the financial and time blindness that people living with ADHD experience.

Taking money from my account . 19th Dec 2024 I looked at this app and the half way through the questionnaire I realised I cannot afford this. Sadly I must have gone too far through the process and they charged me.  I emailed them and was told I would not be charged.   

I have been charged monthly and have never used the app.  Getting help is impossible.  Once you find the request help form online, you are forced to only choose from selected problems that didn’t fit my issue.  The. You can only type 250 characters and 1 file.  

I got a response days later and all they did was refund me $2.99, said they have stopped the subscription and then closed the ticket. There was no opportunity for me to talk to someone to sort this out so I have had to do the same process again.  The money is still coming out of my account! I am in Australia and my bank cannot stop this from reoccurring but they can reverse each payment but I have to call them every month! 

In total they have taken approximately $140 from my account.  The transactions were only and got list in my statement with day to day living transactions until recently.  

I have adhd so that also didn’t help.  

I do not recommend this app for anyone, Let alone someone with ADHD!

Unethical & opaque practises . Do not go near this app unless you want to spend a significant amount of time trying to unsubscribe from a whole bunch of related apps charging you will get charged for on top of the initial outlay. The free trial period is not free and I was charged over a hundred dollars and spent an hour trying to unsubscribe from 6 other in-app subscriptions that I was not advised about and would been charged for. What an unethical app! Terrible not to be transparent to subscribers. As if life isn’t hard enough already for adhd-ers. Shame on you!

Charged after subscription cancelled! . I have been charged $65 despite my trial subscription being cancelled for months.  Despite having DEFINITELY cancelled it during the trial period, which is evident in my “subscriptions list,” the App “help” tells me that there were Terms and Conditions when I signed on that make a refund now - 3 months post-cancellation- that called for auto-renewal, thereby making a refund impossible. I requested the wording from the terms and conditions, was not provided with it and instead told that they would not be discussing it further and the case is closed. I’m actually shocked. The irony that this is an app claiming to help ADHDers while simultaneously acting like ADHD-predators is not lost on me. So furious.

Do not download this app . I tried to cancel my subscription when I realized this app wasn’t the right fit for me. As some previous reviews state there is probably no real customer support I asked for the subscription to be cancelled before the trial ended. It didn’t happen. Not only that but their apps are not synced so I got double charged and they have since ignored any attempts I’ve made to contact them. I’m out nearly $100 for an app I would not recommend to anyone with ADHD do not bother.

Predatory and scammy. Read terms and conditions before you download . I downloaded the app and initiated a trial but within a short period decided that this app isn’t for me (or anyone for that matter). Everything is too confusing and overwhelming and I don’t even have ADHD. I don’t know how horrible it could be for people who do have it. 

However, I decided within a few days that this is not going to work and cancelled the trial. But they still took 40 Euros from without informing me, probably preying on the fact that most people do not read the entire terms and conditions. That is a great business plan. I got to know only today that they have taking money from the account. The app did not in any way support the cancellation of my subscription. I had to go to their website to do it, which would be fine if they had any sort of ethics to inform me that they are taking money from me.

Subscription Scam . Maybe you already Googled it, but this app is a scam. I tried the trial but didnt like it, so I ended my subscription before the trial expired. However, they still withdrew 39,99 euros from my bank account, which left me confused.

When I checked my Apple subscriptions, I couldn’t see any active subscriptions it said my subscription had ended. I didn't understand what was going on, so I had to log in to the website again and contact customer service. I explained the situation, sent them a screenshot, and requested a refund. They responded that they would refund the money, but this is unacceptable.

They are using deceptive tactics to take advantage of people with ADHD. Absolutely cannot recommend.

Giving anxiety from the get go, instead of helping it . I subscribed to a one week trial which I paid for. I wanted to cancel my subscription, because I only wanted to try the app for a week and not get charged for a full month once the week was over.

However I could not find my plan on the website and there was no cancel button. My plan says I have a free subscription, which is not true as I paid for the one week trial.

I also checked my apple subscriptions and I could not cancel there either.

After a while of looking on the website, I was able to submit a ticket to cancel my subscription, but the robot that answered  says that the “current cycle” is canceled. It does not specify the date from which my subscription is canceled from. So now I am gonna be sitting here for a week being anxious about my subscription being canceled. I truly hope that it did get canceled. Hard to confirm this with a robot as it gave a sandard repeating answer to all my questions.

The UI and the website are confusing. Subscription status should be more clear and cancel button should be there at all times.

I think this app is praying on people with ADHD and makes their subscription hard to cancel so we forget it and they can charge us more money. 

Absolutely do not recommend and I am not even interested anymore in trying the app.

Be careful with your credit card . I have not signed up for Premium and it took money from my account twice, almost 70 euros. There was no way to unsubscribe from the phone as with all other Apple Pay subscriptions. Definitely not adhd friendly and a little scammy I’d say.

Subscription trap scam that monetizes adhd absent mindedness . The app actually does not work at all. The menu is frozen and I cannot navigate at all. I cannot to to settings or use it otherwise. Even if it actually worked as it did at first, it is absurdly expensive.

Moreover, I cannot unsubscribe this terribly expensive app. There is no way for me to unsubscribe from app as it does not work. I cannot unsub from the app store either. When I log in from the website it says I have premium BUT THE UNSUB BUTTON IS NOT RESPONSIVE. There is no way this is not a designed feature. 

Do not fall for the free trial scam. They hope you sub, forget it or give up trying to unsub.

do not recommend . was completely unaware that i had subscribed to the premium service as it did not even show up on my app store subscriptions, was very shocked when they charged me over £30 months after i had downloaded it and used the app once

another mental health app that seems to be focused on profiting off of vulnerable people

update: they have actually charged me a total of over £70 which i was completely unaware of, absolutely awful app built around scamming people with ADHD and other mental health issues.

this is a scam . honestly i feel overwhelmed using this for an app designed for adhd. they offer pricing subscription right off the bat as well. which i cancelled and yet it still charged me every month which is irritating though i’ve blocked the payment. how to deal with this???

Preying on vulnerable people . After seeing ads for this app dozens of times every day presenting itself as the solution for people struggling with ADHD, designed by academics, I caved and said I’d try it for just under a pound. As a disabled and chronically ill person, I do not have a lot of money to spare on something that won’t even really tell me what it is and simply promises to change my life. Instead of learning more during the sign-up process, I mostly remember it just being a series of upsells for yet more vague apps and subscriptions.
I did my best to find how to decline the upsell again and again and when I finally got to try out the app, I quickly realised that it would not work for me. Before being able to do anything else, you need to make a solemn promise to yourself that includes remembering every day that you are going to die. I do not need that kind of anxiety trigger and it suggested a vibe of pressure to be productive to me that is not compatible with taking care of my mental health while chronically ill.
I ended up deleting the app and thought that was that until I see a month later that 35 pounds have been taken from my bank account. I was not aware of committing to a subscription that would 40x in price between month 1 and 2 and I did not receive any communication in advance of the renewal or debiting my account. In order to find how to cancel the subscription, I had to re-download the app and go through another five-minute tutorial before being able to navigate to my account settings.
As an app that advertises relentlessly to people with ADHD who are struggling, not sending any heads up and then making the process so convoluted reads as clearly predatory to me.

Fraudulent and Takes Advantage . States nowhere that it will charge you for your ‘free trial’ apart from the £1 pre clicking Apple Pay. A £14.41 payment has been taken from my bank, this isn’t on the apple subscription part, it’s directly from my bank. I have contacted the app and been told it’s a ‘set up fee for the trial period’. Absolutely disgusting considering it’s aimed at people with ADHD who can have difficulties processing certain amounts of information. The info wasn’t there to process anyway! DO NOT TRUST THIS APP.

Feels like a scam - impossible to cancel . I have tried to cancel my subscription several times to no avail. I have contacted support and they said I have an active subscription on my email addresses and can’t cancel it but when I log in with this account no subscription exists yet I continue to be charged. I was even prompted to pay for a pro account when I’ve supposedly already got one? Terrible app and terrible support especially when I originally downloaded it in hope that it would help me with my adhd and instead it has made me even more stressed and overwhelmed

Too much going on, not user friendly . I really wanted to love this app.

I signed up, paying the option of either £0.89p, £9, or £14.99 (or something like that). I honestly thought this was the price of the subscription so was horrified after paying £9 to realise that it would be a £31.99 monthly charge to continue to use the app after the ‘free trial’. So, wasn’t too impressed there.

I then had to navigate through endless pop ups for additional apps (no doubt with their own monthly subscription cost), as well as an incredibly confusing to use user interface with features locked etc. 

I’ve had it for 3 days and have already cancelled the subscription, deleted my account and deleted the app

If you have ADHD, an app I find quite helpful for organisation is called ‘Structured’ as it’s simple to use and not too overwhelming

Theft . I signed up to a very specific single app. But I’ve been charged for a bundle that I never signed up for. Cancelling your subscription requires signing in online. Rather than through the usual apple settings. 

Do Not do their free trial. They will rob you

It’s disgraceful that this is being targeted at those with ADHD

Avoid if you have ADHD . I feel like this app is designed to pray on people with ADHD rather than help them. The sign up process is pushy and offers the world and in return it is difficult to use and even trickier to unsubscribe. 

I tried for a few days and unsubscribed on the app, deleted it from my phone and forgot about it. 

Before I knew it they had taken £60 from my account without any notification or invoice and it took me actual hours to figure out how to unsubscribe fully from the website. I’m 29 and consider myself tech savvy but navigating this was incredibly frustrating. 

I have now paid an obscene amount of money for an app I used for 3 days and then deleted and the customer service is very ‘computer says no’. 

I wouldn’t bother trying.

STEALING MY MONEY FOR THE LAST MONTH DESPITE CANCELLING . Since cancelling the app at the end of October - the fabulous have tried to charge me twice (so two separate amounts for no reason )
A total of 14 times - which is every other day since the 4th November 2024.

I have no clue at all why I’m being charged and why it’s two amounts every other day for the entire of this month.

They are charging me:
£23.99
AND a second amount of
£34.99

A total of £707.76
Which is absolutely outrageous and incredibly unprofessional- let alone the fact I have serious ADHD which this app claims to help with.

I’ve wrote in and have no explanation as to why this is happening and why this will not be stopped.
I do not have the money for this complete scam of an app - and from looking at the comments on instagram I’m not the only person! 

This is causing me so much stress when I am
already dealing with an immense amount in my life - I subscribed to this app in good faith but have had this app try to bleed my funds dry.

Chaotic . I bought a subscription to Clarify from Instagram and then ended up with this app? It was such a chaotic looking app I immediately closed it and only realised they’d given me this, not the app I’d though I was getting when I was cancelling the subscription. Turns out I was going to be charged for both this app and clarify. Seems like a con to get people with ADHD into something they’ll likely immediately forget about. Bit gross.

Scam do not download . I did not subscribe to this app I was literally considering a trial and looking at the site when I saw that £56.99 was pending from my bank account. I have contacted support and cancelled the subscription that was opened without my authorisation. I have also cancelled the personal coaching as had also not requested this. Avoid this app at all costs. The app is extremely annoying and it is almost impossible to contact support. It preys on those of us with ADHD I am disgusted with my experience 

.

Don’t bother. . I had this for about 10 minutes, cancelled my subscription and deleted the app. 

I was sucked in by seeing a short quiz about ADHD types, as I feel I could be suffering with ADHD and SPD I thought I’d try it, more information I have the better whilst I’m building up the courage to talk to my doctor. 

I answered the questions and signed up to the 89p trial as I was more interested in the results of my answers, what I actually got was totally unexpected, unwanted and made me immediately hate the app. 

I was immediately forced into another quiz and asked a range of questions, answered this thinking they were baseline sign up questions and I’d see my results after. No such luck, instead I got pushed into a “journey” which I didn’t want. 

I already get outside professional help with my nutrition, exercise and mobility as well as I’ve recently undergone surgery; I didn’t ask to be set goals and the app asked nothing about me. I tried to browse around after I’ve got past the annoying amount of pop ups and again, nothing useful or any results from the first quiz I did. 

Also found it very rigid as it asked me what habits I already did… I selected one as there was no option to skip or say that I didn’t do any of the habits which would’ve been the truth. 

Rubbish app unless you fit into their perceived boxes, willing to follow their process with no question and have no issues with being told what to do and when.

App deducted money from my bank account without consent . I downloaded it just to try out and deleted shortly after. A few weeks later it deducted 90$ from my account and it turned out I was subscribed to two of their packages, although I never answered their emails about confirming any subscriptions. Even after cancelling and starting refound process today it tried to take money from my account again. I searched online and multiple people had these same issuses with them. It is a real working app like all the other ADHD scheduling apps, but with these non consensual automatic payments it’s as close to a scam as it gets. They refound the payments if you contact them but still very sketchy.

The worst app if you have ADHD . I found an ad of this app in instagram and decided to try. I did registration and paid 1$ for trial for 14 days. I created account, downloaded the app and met a lot of difficulties to login. I spent 10 min to understand how it works. App stuck on email confirmation. When i finally received the link for email confirmation it asked me to do new registration. Now I don’t know how to cancel this subscription bcs for all this time with this app I received a lot of stress and my ADHD just hit me up. Stress stress stress.

Watch out it is scam . they use desperate attempts to help people with adhd by advertising that they improve their lives and let you try the premium version for $1. I tried it, canceled my subscription, and today I saw that 300 PLN was deducted from my account, because I supposedly signed up for it. I had to join the subscription when switching to premium in fabulous, but I was not informed about it when I canceled. I made sure of it when canceling my subscription and I think it is a shameless scam. I am losing a lot of money and didn't even use these apps… scammers

Borderline Scammers . They claim to help ADHD, but no one with ADHD is safe to use this app without feeling like they were pulled a fast one.
I downloaded and PAID in several steps while using Fabulous. I did it because I wanted an efficient solution for my ADHD. One week after using it I realized it wasn’t helping me at all and tried to cancel my free trial subscription where ALL subscriptions are canceled - the IPhone Settings. Fabulous doesn’t show up there at all. 2 weeks go by and I was charged almost 96€ from this app. Fortunately they processed my refund very quickly when I asked for one. But still I had a terrible experience with the app and truly believe Fabulous is taking advantage of people with ADHD.

Be carfeul with subscription . I cancelled the premium subscription and they took my money either way because cancelling lower plan means they automatically upped my subscription to a 4 months!!! The worst app ever. And it is supposed to be for people with ADHD but cancelling plan is almost impossible. I am sad and honestly could not afford all the money it took me away

The billing practices of this app should be illegal—hundreds of dollars of duplicate bills . The alarming thing about this app is that it promotes itself as ADHD support then discretely makes multiple frivolous debit card charges that someone with ADHD is less likely to notice happening. Then it creates a tedious hours-long process to correct the matter or unsubscribe from accounts if you want to stop being billed, knowing that many people with ADHD will be too exhausted to go through that. 

wish I could attach a screenshot of my bank statement in which 15 out of the last 20 transactions are duplicate unauthorized charges made by this company long after I canceled my subscription. Even when I signed up they claimed the fee was a monthly charge, but they try to charge me twice a week. 

Here’s what happened. I was signed up for this app for less than 5 minutes before the first duplicate credit card charges started rolling in. The first round was three identical $25 signup charges, which meant they billed me $75, three times what I authorized. I realized my mistake and canceled my account. But—days later, they charged me $75 again in three separate $25 transactions. 

The company simply directs you to their opaque unsubscribe process, saying they won’t stop billing you unless you unsubscribe in the *exact same way* that you signed up. There are several signup methods and they aren’t able to say which one you used. There is no other support that they provide. Unfortunately, unsubscribing is not an option because, according to their systems, I already canceled my subscription. There seem to be multiple ghost accounts I have no access to, there is no way to identify what signup method they think I used so that I could unsubscribe by that process. 

Ultimately, I had to close the bank account they were billing me at, which, again, takes valuable time. But I still get weekly fraud alerts from my bank notifying me this company is still trying to bill the debit card which no longer exists. 

I believe this type of business practice is illegal in my state, and I have reported them, but it needs to be a federal crime.

Speechless . TL,DR: I do not recommend you download this app. I do not recommend you provide this app with your credit card information. This app has many bugs. This app promises too many simultaneous features and will leave you confused as to what you did in the app. This app prompts you to purchase many additional apps all at once. This app hurt my brain and made me dumber for using it. This app made me financially poorer (even though it’s a free trial). It’s like the D0n@lď Tr¥^^p of apps. Do not—I repeat, do not—take the five star reviews seriously. They simply cannot be real. Have a fine day. 

>>>Fabulous is without doubt the most convoluted & confusing app I think I’ve ever tried using.

Found about this online and took their questionnaire. I agreed to their free trial outside of the app (DO NOT DO THIS!!!) and used Apple’s HideMyEmail feature to protect my anonymity. 

I immediately found myself on a webpage asking for a small fee to pay their people for the “free trial.” I am nice and apparently gullible because I stupidly agreed. Then they sent me to a page that asked me to ¿sign up for other apps? At additional fees? And separate trial periods? Like… I was SOOOO lost! 

So, I downloaded the app and tried signing in… which was a nightmare. It asked me if I wanted to subscribe and stuff despite me providing my email address/username. This got me to thinking that maybe I agreed to one of Fabulous’s sister apps and maybe I didn’t even know what I was trying to do! Then I couldn’t sign into the original website without having to retake the questionnaire again! I finally found a login page which required email verification. I push the button in the email and get directed to the beginning of the questionnaire… AGAIN! 

I honestly have no idea HOW I FINALLY got into the app, but I did. It prompted me to tap on a play icon overlaying a pretty picture of some dude ¿rafting? ¿I think? Which brought me to a list of things me and Fabulous’s little sprites would set out to accomplish. Cute. I pushed on a button… nothing. Couldn’t go back. Couldn’t go forward. I closed the app and HAD TO GO THROUGH THE ENTIRE SIGN IN AGAIN. Did it… bc I’m patient and kind. Landed again on the rafting guy then the list then the nothingness. Redownloaded the app. Same thing. Downloaded one of their sister apps. Couldn’t make heads or tails of it. Finally, in this app, it brought me to a water counting page… because, in order to learn good habits, you must start by counting cups of water… you know…like every other self-help app? 

In the midst of this, my credit card company who could care less about a $1000 out of the blue charge to a kayak company in the middle of the Serengeti called repeatedly until I finally answered asking if I legit made this $10 purchase. That, too, was an absolute nightmare.

I canceled my subscription (I think? Lots of people here say they did too but got hoodwinked and charged later anyway). 

I do not recommend this app. I REALLY do not recommend providing your credit card information to this thing. This app did not help my ADHD and made me feel a certain kind of crazy that I was not aware that I am so capable of.

Predatory Pricing Structure . Update: After contacting support as directed in the developer response, I was told:

“At the time of purchase, the renewal date and billing details were provided, and it was stated that the trial or subscription automatically renews unless it's cancelled at least 24 hours before the renewal date.”

Basically, “sucks to be you, we already got your money.” This seemed like an AI generated support response, and wasn’t actually relevant to my request. The relevant portion of the response was that the charges were just non-refundable.

So, if you actually have ADHD, this company is absolutely predatory, you will be subjected to literally five different upcharges if you try to sign up for the trial, all of which appear identical! And some of which sign you up for ADDITIONAL, SIGNIFICANT monthly recurring charges. Just stay away from these people. Nasty, preying on people like that.

Original: 

It sounds like a great app and idea, and then you go to sign up… First, there’s no free trial, and you’re guilted into paying for a two week trial and sign up to the $20/month membership automatically afterward. After you accept, there are five(!) additional upsell pop up screens that you have to click through, that all look quite similar. So I did the second one, thinking that it was confirming the regular membership. Nope, $10 worth of PDFs, and ANOTHER $20/month “bundle” membership.

Then there are like four more screens asking for money! And probably additional memberships! Like, how much do you expect people to pay you? $100 up front for the trial and $100/month for all the “content” offered?

For an app that claims to take care of people with ADHD, this is absolutely predatory, right out of the gate. Enjoy the $26 you scammed out of me, cancelled immediately.
No . This app is way too busy for someone with ADHD. Also. I canceled my membership and they CONTINUE to charge.

SCAM!!!! . I have tried to cancel my subscription every which way, done charge backs, tried changing my payment method and filed fraud claims with my bank & with apple support  and this app keeps charging me. Sometimes TWICE monthly. NEVER EVER SUBSCRIBE. This company should be reported, I am furious and have spent hours trying to prevent them from continuing to steal from me. Especially for someone with ADHD this is incredibly hard to manage and I’m sure that they know their demographic and seem happy to exploit. Don’t let these scum bags rob you, never ever ever EVER download this app unless you want to be giving them $40-$80 a month for the rest of your life.

Do not even consider this app . Continuously trying to charge my card after I cancelled my subscription, luckily my bank declines the charges. This is happening to many people, search their web reviews. To do this to people with ADHD is the absolute scummiest.

Obnoxious . This is the most ridiculous, overstimulating app and can’t believe they recommend it for ADHD.  I paid $1 to check it out through Apple Cash so that I didn’t enter a cc #.  2 weeks later they charged my Apple Cash $39.99.  DON’T FALL FOR IT

Double charging scam!!!! . I canceled my subscription multiple times through the app. After a few months I realized it wasn’t canceled, and was actually DOUBLE CHARGED for multiple months. After emailing with proof as well and asking for at least a partial refund, I was denied. This app isn’t going to cure your adhd, it’s just going to take your money because your adhd mind will forget about your subscription. And then they will double charge you. Just skip it.

Overwhelming and crazy charges . I’m extremely disappointed with this app. I canceled my subscription and still ended up being charged $39.99. The trial and billing system feels misleading, and judging by other reviews this seems to happen to a lot of people. It honestly feels like the company is taking advantage of users. Also, the app itself is overwhelming, if you have ADHD there is just way too much going on and it’s difficult to use. Overall a very frustrating experience and I would not recommend it.

THIS IS A SCAM DO NOT GET . I got this app in November fo one day. This app asks for a $1 payment as a trial, I canceled the subscription and never used the service, but it charged me $40! I originally thought it was a mistake on my end turns out it had signed me up for the entire package, which I did not do. I made sure I canceled it but it still kept charging me. It is so insidious how they market this app to help people with ADHD but they are looking to scam them instead.

Do not get this app. Esp if you have adhd. . Tried app in September, didn’t work. Many bugs, difficult to understand what the app is actually doing for you. Never used it again. Noticed in December that they had been charging me 2x a month since September. Disputed charged thru app and thru credit card. Received confirmation from app via email that they had canceled my subscription. Except, they charged my credit card again in January. Its giving predatory

Trapped & can not cancel . I attempted to trial this as I have ADHD & was looking for a solution. I paid…and read the fine print. I immediately followed my payment with a cancellation to prevent future billing without consent. This app is so expensive and will charge monthly. My cancellation was disregarded, and now I’m stuck with it attempting to bill me. I didn’t even get to enjoy the trial due to the stress of knowing this would happen. My advice would be not to try it, unless you are prepared to sign up.

unauthorized charges . This company/app has a history of unauthorized charges to its users. I cancelled my subscription entirely and was still charged $40 out of nowhere. I had to dispute this with my bank. Really scummy considering this app targets people with ADHD and executive dysfunction. Reported to the BBB

Predatory Subscription . This app is creepy and I don't like it. I have autism and ADHD and downloaded it on a whim, opened it, saw all of the pop ups and tutorials, and immediately got overwhelmed. I think I paid a couple dollars to "try it out" and then it charged my card for a premium subscription the next month once I had already forgotten about it. After ignoring the app and its repetitive notifications for about two months without opening it, I finally fought my task avoidance enough to open it and cancel my subscription. This took like ten minutes for me to do, because it's hidden in a menu, and it pulls up a pop-up within the app that I couldn't access with my VPN on, so I had to turn that off. And the app has so many pop-up tutorial and other notifications that I kept having to swipe away. Once I finally found the correct settings to cancel my membership, the first time I tried to, it only paused it for two months. I had to click through the entire cancel screen (with an offer to keep my membership for a lower price, which also gave me The Ick) to properly get rid of my membership and promptly uninstall the app. If you actually have a mental disability on the level of ADHD and/or autism, I would highly advise you not to install this app like I did, because of these predatory behaviors. It unsettles me greatly that this app is designed the way that it is for a demographic of people that are usually much more susceptible to falling into traps like these.

DO NOT INSTALL . I tried this app in Nov 2024 for the free trial period. It was fine, but I’ve had better experiences on other apps that I stuck with for longer and didn’t think it was worth the $40/month. The ADHD tax is high enough without another forgotten subscription. 
So… I canceled the subscription before the trial period was even over. 
I’ve since been charged five different times over the last year by this app, each time going through the process of contacting them, my card company, and back and forth to get the $40 charge removed. The most recent charge was Nov 2025, a year after I canceled the trial…never having actually committed to the subscription.

Misleading Payment Model . The app itself works acceptably well for habit-building and has a pretty UI to draw you in. However, I cannot recommend the app as their subscription model is misleading and intentionally hard to cancel. I was advertised a $1 subscription, and then received a $40 payment a few weeks later. I thought I cancelled the plan immediately after and then deleted the app, only to find another $40 charge today 3 months later. In the cancellation process today, they only allowed me to cancel my subscription after jumping through 4-5 different windows trying to re-sell me the subscription I already had, change to a monthly plan instead, etc. Based off of the other reviews, I clearly am not the only person who has had this problem.

I can’t help but feel like with Fabulous’s marketing and their main demographics, their aim is to set up a Planet Fitness-style model where they make money from people struggling with ADHD by tricking people into keeping their subscriptions going. As an alum from the dev’s school (which was a major part of the advertising I saw for the product), it is disappointing to see questionable financial models be the focus for what could be a genuinely helpful app.

It’s subscriptions selling subscriptions . It’s starts off with what I thought was good intentions. Then you are bombarded with subscriptions to other things. It’s so bad to the point I just spent 40 dollars on this app after I thought I cancelled it, only to find it was some focus music spin off from the app. If you think about it, they leveraged your ADHD to get you into other subscriptions. They got me for 39.99. Beware going into this.

Keep charging $$$ despite a canceled subscription . There is something about this app and its operation that is totally sketchy. I am not talking about the content of the app, which I am not a fan of, since I used it for the seven-day free trial in 2023. Since then they have been continuing to charge my credit card despite me canceling the service and sending notes to them in the app that I don't want to use the subscription and reimburse me (probably one or two days after the seven-day trial period). Not only did they not reimburse me the first time but they have been keeping charging me and I have to spend hours with my credit card company to dispute these charges! This is a shame since your app is designed for people with ADHD and it seems your business model is to take advantage of adhd people as they are the most likely ones to miss canceling a trial and then keep charging them as they do not check their credit cards day to day. Shame on you!

DO NOT GET THIS APP . This app is a complete scam, beware!!!! It starts with a free subscription and then they want you to pay $40/two months. I cancelled my free subscription 2 days before the renewal date and everything seemed fine, the screen confirmed I cancelled the subscription and even tried to offer me a deal to come back. On what would’ve been the renewal date, I got charged $40 AND weirdly got an email at the exact same time confirming the cancellation of my subscription but listed my cancellation request date as tomorrow (the day after the renewal date, not the actual date I cancelled it, 2 days before receiving the email). So i checked back in my profile and it showed that the subscription hadn’t been cancelled at all and I was on an active subscription. To make it worse, customer service is allusive and messages have character limits so I can’t even fully explain what happened. The irony is this app is marketed to people with issues like ADHD, which makes me feel like all of this is very predatory, like they’re hoping we won’t be able to follow through with all this mess of cancelling. Beware, do not get this app! It’s a trap!

Tricky thievery . This app appears to be high-quality app and I’m surprised that it has so many stars and was an editor’s choice for Apple because they charged my account and I did not even subscribe to anything and would never have intention intentionally subscribe to anything because it’s out of my budget. I would never have subscribed to this app no matter how beautiful it looks or how useful it pretends to be whether or not it’s useful I wouldn’t know I wouldn’t use an app like this because I use list that I make because it helps me more. So now I have to go into a big hassle of a situation that I don’t have time energy or the mental capacity to be able to deal with right now on top of everything else that I deal with as a differently-abled person. They know this because they are advertising to people with ADHD. And things that are similar so they know it’s hard to navigate complex websites to get the help you need to get your money back or get them to turn off your subscription. I literally never subscribed to this app and they are charging me now.. It doesn’t show up on my Apple apps charges. It shows up on my PayPal account. But they are literally stealing from the poor and differently-abled people.

Impossible to cancel pricy subscription. Be careful. . The app is alright, another habit tracker that is useful but I’ve given it a 1 star review because it’s impossible to cancel. I had to close my bank account because they continued to charge me. I don’t have access to the email I initially signed up with so there is no way for me to actually cancel my subscription. They have the app and a website along with other sister apps that are advertised (I also subscribed to clarify unfortunately) just burn your money instead because you can’t just cancel through subscriptions like most apps. There’s like a 10 step process and a different website you have to go to in order to manage your subscription. God forbid you forget your password…like most ADHD people 🙄 because you’ll never be able to cancel. 

I’ve been through the runaround with support and they told me there was nothing they could do so my only option to keep them from charging me forever was to close the bank account it was attached to. Seems like the high pricing model and the overly complex subscription management is geared towards people with mental health problems that will forget so they can keep raking in the subscription fees while we forget or get too overwhelmed with the complexity of canceling. Definitely a scam in my opinion.

DO NOT GET THIS APP . The app is intentionally confusing and preys on ADHD people that will get too overwhelmed with the app and forget about it. It also charged me for something I didn’t sign up for, and charged me after I cancelled my subscription! It’s a scam and the layout is the opposite of that what people with ADHD need.

I paid $1 for a free trial & they took the $1 but didn’t give me 14 days . I got the 14 day trial for a $1. When I went to change my subscription so I wouldn’t get charged automatically at the end, they took away the remaining days, so… the 14 day free trial is a scam. Plus, they always want you to download more and more apps. 🤯 not good for adhd brain after all

Trapped into $320 of charges . I tried this app, it wasn’t for me. When I canceled my subscription, I kept getting charged. I didn’t notice until I saw my credit card bill later. I reached out for help, but was unable to get any clarity on why I was being charged. This went on for months. They were asking for lots of information that I couldn’t find, all I could see was that I was being charged, and the charges kept coming. Eventually, they were able to find that I was being charged through an alternate email address- maybe something to do with google logins? They finally stopped the charges from keeping on coming, and would only refund the most recent month. In the end, after I had already canceled and received confirmation of canceling the app, I was still charged $320 cumulatively ($40/mo for 8 months) for an app that I didn’t use and had canceled. For someone trying to manage ADHD, what a hilarious and terrible and expensive trap!

Predatory Company . I downloaded this app because it seemed to have all the bells and whistles. I was considering some of the linked apps and starting reading reviews. Many users complained that the app was distracting and and spent more time to set up and use than time saved. They also complained that subscription fees were charged even when cancelled and it was difficult to get refunds. I went through all the steps to cancel my subscription and delete my account, yet I received notification that I was charged $49.99. I was so incensed that I addressed the issue immediately. Had I not had the chance to take care of it right away, given my ADHD, this may have gotten buried under other demands and I would be out $$$ for nothing. Not right at all!

Charges and subscribes you automatically . In typical ADHD style, i only used this app once. Apparently i subscribed to the Premium service, probably i forgot to unsubscribe to a free trial. Thats fine i wasted about $80, lesson learned. However,  a month later, it subscribed me to a $60 bi-monthly subscription which i never even set eyes on and withdrew a cumulative $200 before i was able to realize what was going on.

Don't expect customer service . I messaged CS to get clarification about my subscription, b/c I had received several different pieces of info. Their response was only into my account to look. Obviously, I was told many things, so I couldn't do that! Luckily, iPhones keep that info, & I was able to find it there. I deleted the subscription before the end of the trial & was still charged a week later! I sent two methods of proof of the deleted subscription & asked for my money back. They replied & refunded me, saying they had terminated my subscription. I had already done that & had proof! I don't think this company knows what they're doing or has any customer service skills. AND it made my anxiety worse, with so much required reading each day. Not very efficient requiring an ADHD person daily reading material. Buyer beware!

If you have ADHD, beware! . A common quality of apps that target people with ADHD is to sign them up to a subscription (often in a misleading way) and make it hard to cancel. This app is no exception. I was signed up for a subscription when it made it seem like I was declining multiple times. You can’t cancel your subscription through the app. 

ADHD tax is real and they know it. They’re banking on it. Whatever useful qualities this app may have is completely undermined by their shady approach to subscriptions in order to take advantage of the challenges many people with ADHD have with managing subscriptions.

Predatory app . I tried the donation based trial and after a few days knew I would not be using this app beyond the trial. It’s not for me. Lo and behold I see I’m charged $40 for a premium membership that I can’t even cancel on the app. I’m beyond upset as there was no clear indication that I would be charged automatically. It is truly an irony that an app designed to “help” with ADHD would take advantage of “out of sight out of mind” habits for profit. Save some time, money, and energy and work with an actual therapist rather than this late capitalistic hellscape of an app.

Keeps trying to auto renew . This app! Not only did it not understand things like, having kids, but it did not understand wanting to cancel a subscription. I cancelled my subscription last February - this is the third time they’ve tried to fraudulently charge me! This is getting really, really old. They know we have adhd, they know we’re going to forget… it’s not a bug, it’s a feature.

Might be great, feels scammy . Found this app thru an Instagram ad. I was intrigued & signed up for the $1 trial. Although (shoutout ADHD) I never created my account or activated my trial. I *did* however set a reminder & check everywhere I thought of to ensure I wouldn’t be charged when the trial ended! It wasn’t until months later (sifting thru my bank charges) that I realized I was being charged the WHOLE time. Both for the 1 program/app I did the trial for AND a whole separate one I never ever signed up for. That whole time, I never got an invoice, no record of my subscription (besides that initial trial email that explicitly said “MUST CLICK HERE TO ACTIVATE TRIAL” which I never clicked). Leaving lots of details out, but I reached out to customer service & they were no help at all & did not listen to me or the evidence I presented. Was a total of $140 from just November to Feb. Ridiculous. Plus started getting a TON of promo emails from them after reaching out to customer service?? Either way, no way an APP is worth that much. Plus terrible customer service and no way to talk to someone on the phone. Super disappointed & I’ve never left a review before this

Predatory Practices . Highly recommended not downloading this app or falling for the 14 day trial scam. I wanted to try Clarity and signed up for the trial. Without my knowledge they signed me up for the bimonthly subscription for Fabulous too. I didn’t love Clarity and canceled my subscription before the trial ended without realising I had to cancel a whole other subscription for Fabulous that was billing me $50 bimonthly. As a company with a target audience of people with ADHD that have a hard time dealing with things like canceling subscriptions this all feels very predatory and calculated. I am very disappointed and will not ever use any of their services again.

Unauthorized charge . I canceled the trial period days before it was meant to charge for the monthly subscription. It still charged me and when I reached out to their “customer service” they said they would refund the money back to my account. It’s been months and there still hasn’t been a refund. I reached out to them a few times given the excuse of first taking up to 10 days and then 20, all depending on my bank situation? I’ve never experienced a delay in a refund because of my bank. Don’t fall for this app if you’re not actually committed to fully subscribing. 
I would suggest to use that money and get a time management coach in person or through tele health if you have ADHD or just need time management guidance in general.

Literally stole my money . Unfortunately I signed up for this app and to see what it was about a year ago. When I signed up they didn’t have a subscription model, rather you could contribute what you wished to show appreciation for the app. I donated $16 dollars and was told in the app that this was not a subscription and I wouldn’t be charged again. I wish I had the foresight then to screenshot where it said that because it all went down hill from there. I was then charged the next month and every three months after that for $40 plus an international charge. I saw the charge come in September las year and asked for a refund in October. They responded to my first email and then ignored me after I provided my details. When I saw in December I was charged and not only that no one refunded the charges. I reached back out and finally threw a fit when I was charged in March of this year. I was told they could only refund my March charge. And look I’m not a monster I’m not trying to get all my money back but I just want the money back from the time I reached the first time when my request was ignored. That was not my fault and now they continue to ignore me. Really disappointed and not how someone should do business. Told me they’re really in it for the money not actually helping anyone with ADHD… disappointing

Unfortunate customer service . This was advertised to me on ig as a wonderful way to work w my adhd, and having spent a lot of time trying out different apps for such things, I have a system for canceling trials in a timely manner. I remember cancelling,  and reviewed my last billing cycle on my bank statement, checked to make sure I didn’t still have an active account, explained the situation to customer service, and they basically told me I was screwed for using an app for about 3 days. I didnt find anything particularly different than other apps that promise to improve your life, and wondered why the cancellation process or terms would be so counterintuitive for someone with adhd. Something clearly went wrong and the faq to double check if I was in the wrong didn’t help at all- I had no active subscriptions listed on any of the options I could have used, and when I opened the app to double check I had indeed cancelled- it brought me to the initial set-up page as if I’d never even tried it at all. Something clearly went, I assumed cancellation. Then saw a 69.99 charge on my bank statement. Cannot in good faith recommend even to try for those that haven’t tried anything else in this app category due to horrible customer service. It’s predatory and unfair, and now I have to wait to dispute a charge that doesn’t make any sense for a subscription I cancelled and cant log into.  Stay awayyyyyy

Scams ADHD strugglers . This app was a total scam.  As someone struggling with ADHD tendencies I downloaded this app with positivity and quickly told some friends about it!  However then I got the first bill for $16 and thought “oh well I was willing to help cover cost for the trials so it’s ok”.  Then the app asked if I wanted to use sister apps - by the end of the month I was charged $39.99 for one and $29.99 for another app I couldn’t even get to work and when I asked about canceling and getting my money back, I was told forgetting to cancel wasn’t covered for a refund.  I was in the Palisades fire, cancelling a “free” subscription was the last thing on my mind.  If there’s any chance you’ll forget to cancel avoid this app at all costs.

Convoluted . I would give 0 stars if I could. Despite never activating the subscription via an email sent when I first signed up, I was still charged, and when I contacted customer support, they couldn’t locate my account (because it wasn’t activated). I had already canceled all my Apple subscriptions in Apple Subscriptions” on my phone including Fabulous, months ago when I first signed up, and my account showed that the subscription would end in November. However, the app didn’t specify a year, leading me to believe it was November 2024—when in reality, I can only assume it meant November 2025. If I had already paid and canceled, why am I still being charged monthly? This isn’t a contract requiring a full-year commitment. If the subscription is canceled, payments should stop. Customer service was unhelpful, despite the app claiming to offer refunds for users who “forget to cancel”, which is misleading for an app marketed as ADHD-friendly. In addition to all of these the app is and all of its sister apps are difficult to navigate and not user friendly considering its intended audience. I would not recommend this app (or any of its sister apps) to anyone especially those with ADHD.

Not great for people with ADHD . I paid the subscription on the website instead of on my iPhone, which was a huge mistake because then it does not show up on the list of subscriptions on your phone and you would have to track it independently. 

Since I didn’t realize it wasn’t in my subscriptions list on my phone, I didn’t unsubscribe in time, and the app developer would not refund my subscription even though I had not used it for months before the automatic renewal.

In the past I have found other app developers to be kind enough to refund subscription fees when I forget to unsubscribe. Not this one. You would think that an app that is supposed to help people with ADHD would be much more understanding!

Don’t pay $$ for apps that purport to help neurodiverse folks but rather prefer to take advantage. . I am posting this review/warning under both the Fabulous AND Clarify app pages because it is the developer’s dishonest method of not appropriately handling these charges of getting BOTH apps that created this issue.

I want to warn everyone against subscribing to any product offered by Fabulous, an app that purports to help people with ADHD but seems to better practice taking advantage of what can be attributed at least in part to symptoms of ADHD and neurodiversity.

I decided in November to take advantage of the free trial offered. As part of the on boarding, I was also offered a free trial of another app designed by Fabulous supposedly even more targeted to ADHD, an app called Clarify.

I found neither app really worked for me that well, or at least, they didn’t draw me in enough to want to use them. That’s fine—every brain is different, and everyone has different things that may/may not work for them.

Before my free trial ended, I logged in to my account to cancel, and yes, my Fabulous account WAS in fact canceled, and I received confirmation. I looked for information about Clarify, but there was nothing separate, nor did I receive any separate notifications from Fabulous OR Clarify stating that a separate trial was ending and I would be charged.

After canceling, I did not go into either app again.

But recently, I noticed a charge on my credit card from the same day I cancelled by trial. The charge was listed on my statement as “FABULOUS APP PARIS” and was for $29.99. The cancellation email only offers instructions on how to reactivate your subscription; it offers no information or warning about any other subscriptions or apps. In fact, while it tells you how to reactivate, it does NOT even have a single hyperlink connected to any support or account pages.

When I went to look for how to get back into the account page (as I had actually purchased the subscription directly from within the app, and it did not go through the App Store or my apple account, even though I had logged in using Apple), I had to find the original activation email which had a link to my account page. When I finally clicked that link today, I suddenly saw the Clarify account and it showed that it was still active.

I immediately cancelled the account and then searched for a way to contact them to request a refund for this amount that I did not believe I should have been charged, and that was connected to an account that I had never used since I believed I had canceled it at the same time as canceling Fabulous.

There is no support email address to contact Fabulous. You simply submit a request through their site. To their credit, they responded to me quickly, but their responses were wholly unsatisfactory, essentially saying, Too bad!

I received a receipt for my initial Clarify subscription, but I have never received any further correspondence nor receipts from them. The only reason I even know about the charge was from my credit card statement, which, again, does not mention “Clarify.” 

There are terms on the receipt email that state, “Please note, if you purchase more than one Fabulous product, other products may be renewing on separate dates and applicable receipts for those products may be sent separately.” However, once I canceled Fabulous, while I received the cancellation confirmation, I never received ANY separate receipt regarding the auto-renewal charge nor did I receive any warning that my trial was ending. I have received nothing from them whatsoever other than their decision not to refund this money.

This is simply horrible customer service. Had I been utilizing the app even a single time after my cancellation of Fabulous or after the renewal date, or had I allowed the auto-renew to happen more than once, I would understand being unwilling to make the consideration. But that is not the case. Their communication is at best lacking, especially charging a credit card without sending an email receipt/notification after. At worst, it is a ploy to grab some extra money for unused services.

I sent three messages back and forth with their support staff before writing this review. After the first refund denial, I wrote that I would post reviews and contest the charge with my credit card company. Instead, their final response to me, written in faux-apologetic language that equates to saying: , We’re so sorry that we can’t offer you this customer consideration because you’re too stupid to have figured out that nuances of our cancellation policies that require separate cancellations for products that you purchased at the exact same time. (That’s not a quotation, but it is what their message essentially says.)

Their final response to me ended with: “This refund request will now be closed, but please do let us know if you need assistance with anything else.”

Either way, this is not a developer that I would ever consider purchasing anything from again., regardless of how interesting a product may look. I would suggest others stay away as well unless you are ready and prepared to skip having a “free trial.” There’s a good chance it won’t turn out to be free.

Predatory scam . I signed up for help with ADHD, the product structure itself was not that useful or supportive to me, which is not a crime. What i
IS criminal is that the subscription costs $40 per month, which was not made clear when I signed up, and the company makes it difficult to cancel as you cannot access your billing info from inside the app. On top of that, I learned that I had been signed up for a $30/month subscription to their app Clarify that I never signed up for. 

It all felt intentionally misleading and like they are preying on people with ADHD joining impulsively and forgetting or not noticing the charges. Based on their responses to the other one star reviews here, I don’t think they care about making a user oriented experience, I think they are content with getting $70 out of people for a few months before they get angry and cancel. I’m not one to leave reviews, and certainly not bad ones, but this was a massive disappointment and made me feel manipulated.

Deceptive Company . I I was being charged for two subscriptions but was unable to even use the premium service because every time I logged in to the app or online it said I was a “free user” which was so confusing. So I have been unable to locate or manage my subscription. I have attempted to contact the care team several times and it’s almost like I’m being ignored. Terrible customer care and especially disappointing for an app designed to assist individuals with ADHD.

DO NOT GET THIS APP . I signed up for a free trial of this app and six months and $450 later I am still being charged even though I’ve cancelled multiple times. They don’t actually cancel your subscription, only pause it for two months and then keep charging you. The only way to cancel is to email them directly by which that point they refuse to give you a refund because you signed their terms and conditions. They make it purposefully confusing and a pain to end your subscription and it’s highway robbery. No matter how good this app may be O never want to support people stealing from their vulnerable clients in this way - many with adhd like me who this kind of thing is what gives us a mental breakdown.

Scam . Update: As you can see the developer’s response but what he fails to mention is that they sent me an email stating they couldn’t find my account at all. So then my question is if I don’t have an account why did they withdraw a subscription fee from my bank account? Again, this is a complete scam and please stay away from this app. 

If I could give 0 stars I would. I downloaded the app thinking it would help me w/ my ADHD on keeping on a schedule. Once I saw it cost money, I closed the app. Some how in that short time they had charged me for going past the 7 day free trial. I requested them to refund and they tell me I don’t have an account but I’ve uploaded a picture from my bank showing that they had taken money. And now I’ve submitted a request for refund every day since and I’ve never heard back. Don’t let these companies scam you b/c they’re praying on ppl w/ disabilities that know they will forget to cancel!! Shame on you and your business.

Review of Customer Service / Ability to Cancel . This product that I don’t use has become a tax I pay for having ADHD thanks to poor customer service. Setting aside the effectiveness of what is certainly an aesthetically pleasing app, once you’re locked in after a trial too short to prove the habit-forming mettle of the app (more likely if you self-identify as someone who struggles with routine and/or ADHD, which makes the lack of compassion and flexibility from customer service more egregious as this is their target audience), will customer service queries be answered in a timely and clear fashion? Not for me. I got a notice of high email volume and the response was delayed. Eventually I was denied a refund for a premium membership in a personal message then an separate notice of a free 90 days on the app (that I don’t find useful and want to cancel) without any context as to why I was receiving it. I hoped the email showed I was restored to trial status and could now cancel, but no, they are bent on keeping my fee. Fine. But the account management system is still leaving me in limbo and feeling powerless to actually manage my account ie, ensure I am never charged again. It takes me in login loops and does not provides clear language confirmation as to HOW I am subscribed nor an easy button to cancel / ensure it won’t auto renew. My advice is to get a bullet journal and not have to deal with the backend confusion of this app and its sister apps which are constantly being internally advertised in it.

Works but triple billed me . I just signed up for it through internet and Apple because they had different prices for each and the monthly, 3 months and yearly price were vastly different.
When I signed up through the internet it prompted 2 week trial with a 3month subscription after the trial at
39.99 every 3 months or a yearly subscription at $59.99. Then when I went to sign up through Apple it said 1 week trial with a 60% off annual price at 19.99 a year. When I did that it prompted me to cancel the Apple subscription and keep the internet one. Obviously I canceled the internet one and kept the Apple one.

However one week later I was charged the 19.99 for the yearly subscription then two weeks later I was charged another 39.99 a few minutes later it tried to charge me 29.99 but my bank flagged it. And now today it actually charged me  the 29.99 it tried to take yesterday. The only subscription I have active is an apple subscription for fabulous for a deal of $19.99 for a year. Please resolve this immediately. This app has helped me with my adhd but not worth the hassle of all these extra charges.

Inaccessibility Predatory & Disappointing . I have never written an app review, but this experience was especially absurd so I felt the need to inform a potential audience about the miscommunication and inaccessibility of this app. I downloaded the app to try out the free trial since I have been wanting to build a better routine. About a week in, I was underwhelmed by the limitations of the start of the “journey” and realized it wasn’t going to be for me, so I decided to cancel the trial. I went into my account information to try and manage my subscription, but only saw an option to delete my entire account. I went ahead and did that, but decided to check the article online about how to cancel the trial in case deleting my account wasn’t enough. It said that if I had started it through the app, I just had to go into my subscriptions page in my apple ID and cancel it there (a process I have done several times before). I went into that page and didn’t see any subscriptions there, so I figured that by deleting my entire account the trial/subscription was thus cancelled. So I thought it was resolved. 

A couple weeks later, I see that my credit card has been charged 40 DOLLARS by the “Fabulous App Paris”. In shock, I submit a refund request explaining my situation. The response I get is that, since I read the Terms and Conditions, I could not be issued a refund. As far as I know, reading the terms and conditions does not preclude one from miscommunication on behalf of the app and any faults in locating the subscription. I was told I had to visit the Fab WEBSITE (which I never had, as far as I can remember) and cancel the subscription from the account page there. In order to prevent further charges, I visited the website and was told I had to ACTIVATE my account in order to access it at all. So not only did I myself know I never used the functionality of the app for which I was charged, the program ITSELF knew this. I went through and officially cancelled my subscription, as well as expressed my disappointment to the app team for their response several days ago. I have yet to receive any response. 

The target audience of this app is, pointedly, individuals with ADHD— me included. Don’t pay $$ for apps that purport to help neurodiverse folks but instead take advantage . I am posting this review/warning under both the Fabulous AND Clarify app pages because it is the developer’s dishonest method of not appropriately handling these charges of getting BOTH apps that created this issue.

I want to warn everyone against subscribing to any product offered by Fabulous, an app that purports to help people with ADHD but seems to better practice taking advantage of what can be attributed at least in part to symptoms of ADHD and neurodiversity.

I decided in November to take advantage of the free trial offered. As part of the on boarding, I was also offered a free trial of another app designed by Fabulous supposedly even more targeted to ADHD, an app called Clarify.

I found neither app really worked for me that well, or at least, they didn’t draw me in enough to want to use them. That’s fine—every brain is different, and everyone has different things that may/may not work for them.

Before my free trial ended, I logged in to my account to cancel, and yes, my Fabulous account WAS in fact canceled, and I received confirmation. I looked for information about Clarify, but there was nothing separate, nor did I receive any separate notifications from Fabulous OR Clarify stating that a separate trial was ending and I would be charged.

After canceling, I did not go into either app again.

But recently, I noticed a charge on my credit card from the same day I cancelled by trial. The charge was listed on my statement as “FABULOUS APP PARIS” and was for $29.99. The cancellation email only offers instructions on how to reactivate your subscription; it offers no information or warning about any other subscriptions or apps. In fact, while it tells you how to reactivate, it does NOT even have a single hyperlink connected to any support or account pages.

When I went to look for how to get back into the account page (as I had actually purchased the subscription directly from within the app, and it did not go through the App Store or my apple account, even though I had logged in using Apple), I had to find the original activation email which had a link to my account page. When I finally clicked that link today, I suddenly saw the Clarify account and it showed that it was still active.

I immediately cancelled the account and then searched for a way to contact them to request a refund for this amount that I did not believe I should have been charged, and that was connected to an account that I had never used since I believed I had canceled it at the same time as canceling Fabulous.

There is no support email address to contact Fabulous. You simply submit a request through their site. To their credit, they responded to me quickly, but their responses were wholly unsatisfactory, essentially saying, Too bad!

I received a receipt for my initial Clarify subscription, but I have never received any further correspondence nor receipts from them. The only reason I even know about the charge was from my credit card statement, which, again, does not mention “Clarify.” 

There are terms on the receipt email that state, “Please note, if you purchase more than one Fabulous product, other products may be renewing on separate dates and applicable receipts for those products may be sent separately.” However, once I canceled Fabulous, while I received the cancellation confirmation, I never received ANY separate receipt regarding the auto-renewal charge nor did I receive any warning that my trial was ending. I have received nothing from them whatsoever other than their decision not to refund this money.

This is simply horrible customer service. Had I been utilizing the app even a single time after my cancellation of Fabulous or after the renewal date, or had I allowed the auto-renew to happen more than once, I would understand being unwilling to make the consideration. But that is not the case. Their communication is at best lacking, especially charging a credit card without sending an email receipt/notification after. At worst, it is a ploy to grab some extra money for unused services.

I sent three messages back and forth with their support staff before writing this review. After the first refund denial, I wrote that I would post reviews and contest the charge with my credit card company. Instead, their final response to me, written in faux-apologetic language that equates to saying: , We’re so sorry that we can’t offer you this customer consideration because you’re too stupid to have figured out that nuances of our cancellation policies that require separate cancellations for products that you purchased at the exact same time. (That’s not a quotation, but it is what their message essentially says.)

Their final response to me ended with: “This refund request will now be closed, but please do let us know if you need assistance with anything else.”

Either way, this is not a developer that I would ever consider purchasing anything from again., regardless of how interesting a product may look. I would suggest others stay away as well unless you are ready and prepared to skip having a “free trial.” There’s a good chance it won’t turn out to be free.

Esperienza pessima e deludente, forse più dell’assistenza clienti . Ho provato Tiimo con una certa curiosità, sperando in uno strumento realmente utile per chi ha bisogno di supporto nell’organizzazione e nella gestione dell’attenzione. In realtà, è stata una delusione totale.

Già da subito non mi ha convinto, tanto che ho smetto di usarla ben prima della fine del periodo di prova gratuita. Nonostante questo, mi è stato addebitato il costo dell’abbonamento, e da lì è iniziata la parte peggiore: l’assistenza.

Li ho contattati tempestivamente, spiegando la situazione con educazione e chiedendo un rimborso per un servizio che non solo non ho usato, ma che non funzionava correttamente fin dall’inizio. La risposta? Fredda, rigida, priva di qualunque empatia. Hanno rifiutato il rimborso in modo sbrigativo e quando ho provato a richiedere se possibile una revisione della decisone inerente la mia richiesta con maggiore chiarezza senza perdere di cortesia, mi è stato risposto in modo barbaro che la decisione è definitiva e non ci sono “i presupposti” per un rimborso. Nessuna traccia di assertività o rispetto che tanto millantano.

La rabbia per l’acquisto è tanta, ma non userò comunque quest’app, perché è davvero mal progettata e inutilizzabile. È assurdo che un’app pensata per aiutare persone con ADHD possa risultare più frustrante del problema stesso. 

Sconsigliata sotto ogni punto di vista: inefficace, instabile e gestita da un’assistenza che non ha alcun interesse reale per i propri utenti.

Not ADHD friendly. Just ADHD targeted. . I downloaded this app because it specifically advertised itself as being ADHD friendly. Unfortunately, my experience was the complete opposite.

The onboarding is filled with endless text and screens to click through, which is already overwhelming. Then you’re encouraged to subscribe with just a couple of taps, but cancelling is an absolute nightmare. Some subscriptions are sold as bundles, others separately, and the cancellation process constantly redirects you between different pages and apps. The layout makes it incredibly easy to accidentally close the page or lose your place and start over.

For an app targeting people with ADHD, this design feels particularly frustrating. It isn’t ADHD friendly at all. If anything, it takes advantage of the exact executive functioning difficulties it claims to help with. Whether intentional or not, the result is the same: cancelling becomes so exhausting that many people may simply give up.

I also found the pricing strategy misleading. The app initially suggests that money shouldn’t stand in the way of improving your life and advertises a plan for around $2. But once you’re invested, you’re presented with subscriptions ranging from $40 to $60. That feels like a bait and switch rather than transparent pricing.

And lastly, loads and loads of AI generated content. For these prices there should be human made content available. 

I genuinely hope the developers reconsider both the subscription flow and the user experience. An app designed for people with ADHD should reduce cognitive load, not increase it.

Once subscribed, figuring out exactly what I had signed up for and how to cancel was a complicated maze. The sheer number of prompts, offers and additional subscription opportunities made the whole experience feel less like onboarding and more like a carefully designed sales funnel.

Having gone through all of that, what I seem to have ended up with is essentially a very expensive reminder to drink water.

I appreciate that subscription apps need to make money, but users should understand clearly when they are making a purchase, what they are purchasing and how much it will cost. In my experience, that clarity was completely lacking.

I would like the subscriptions I inadvertently signed up for through this process cancelled and the charges refunded. I would strongly encourage Fabulous to reconsider an onboarding and payment design that feels particularly inappropriate given the audience it is actively targeting.
